events: I will never forget the first\Nnight I spent far from home.
When I finished twelfth grade,\NI was assigned to Bahir Dar University.
At midday, with just one backpack,\Nseen off by my friend, I left Ankober.
The road was gravel as far as\NDebre Birhan, then asphalt.
Sitting by the window, I watched the\Nforest and the mountain in wonder.
When I reached Lamberet after dark,\Nanother friend was waiting for me.
Addis Ababa met me flooded\Nwith people, lights and cars;
I did not know where to look.
And when we reached Autobus Tera,\Nbrokers surrounded us.
"Do you want a bed? A bed?"\NWe did not know whom to listen to.
In the end we followed one.
it was neither good nor bad;\Nbut it was clean.
Next morning we stood in a long queue\Nand bought the ticket to Bahir Dar.
Today, seven years later, I have one\Nthing to say to all who leave home:
the first night is always confusing.
But the confusion is\Npart of the journey.
Do not run from it; savour it.

cues: When I finished twelfth grade,
I was assigned to Bahir Dar University.
At midday, with just one backpack,
seen off by my friend, I left Ankober.
The road was gravel as far as
Debre Birhan, then asphalt.
Sitting by the window, I watched the
forest and the mountain in wonder.
When I reached Lamberet after dark,
another friend was waiting for me.
Addis Ababa met me flooded
with people, lights and cars;
I did not know where to look.
And when we reached Autobus Tera,
brokers surrounded us.
"Do you want a bed? A bed?"
We did not know whom to listen to.
In the end we followed one.
The room had one bed;
it was neither good nor bad;
but it was clean.
Next morning we stood in a long queue
and bought the ticket to Bahir Dar.
Today, seven years later, I have one
thing to say to all who leave home:
the first night is always confusing.
But the confusion is
part of the journey.
Do not run from it; savour it.
